out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the permit to operate in a conspicuous location.The health permit was not posted in the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. Post the health permit as soon as possible or within 10 days.

violations.title: Food Manager Certificate & Responsibility
violations.observation: There is no Certified Food Manager present in the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager. It is highly suggested that you have more than one employee with the food manager's license. ORS Interactive, Inc. (see handout provided) issues the required photo identification card with proof of successful completion of a certified food manager's exam. Failure to have a certified food manager on site during ALL hours of operation including food preparation, food service, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment/utensils will result in closure of the establishment. Provide a CFM within 10 days.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the food employees, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' The food employees present were not aware of an employee health policy for this establishment.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. The employees present were provided with copies of the FCHD EHP and completed the forms during the inspection after the EHS trained them.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS provided the employees present with a copy of the FCHD V&D cleanup procedure during the inspection.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. A food employee was wearing gloves and sneezed into her gloved hand. She took off the gloves, and put on new gloves without washing her hands first.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The EHS discussed this with the employee and the importance of washing hands in a food establishment.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw shell eggs were stored over tiramisu cake and milk in one of the refrigerators.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The food employee moved the eggs during the inspection to correct.

violations.title: Food Contact Surface, 4 Hour Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: After a conversation with the food employees, it was learned that equipment and utensils are not being cleaned and sanitized at least every 4 hours. Instead, they are only being cleaned at the end of the day and possibly not being sanitized at all.
violations.corrective_action: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils must be cleaned and sanitized at least every 4 hours to prevent contamination by bacterial growth. Clean and sanitize all equipment and utensils before or after use, or at least every 4 hours. The EHS discussed this requirement with the food employees.

violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: The food employee could not provide a food temperature measuring device.
violations.corrective_action: A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. Provide a thermometer capable of measuring the internal temperature of food as soon as possible or before the follow-up on Friday, July 24.

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: the single door refrigerator did not have a thermometer in it.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.Provide thermometers for all refrigerators before the follow-up on July 24.

violations.title: Thermometers, Easily Readable
violations.observation: The temperature measuring device located in/on the following equipment is not designed to be easily readable: the thermometer in the front display case was not working properly and needs to be adjusted.
violations.corrective_action: Temperature measuring devices shall be designed to be easily readable. Adjust the thermometer so that it works properly or install a second thermometer in the unit. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed that clean stainless steel creamer pitchers and spoons were stored on the handsink which exposed the item(s) to contamination.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. Hand sinks are not clean areas. Food and food equipment should not be stored on or near them. Move the equipment to a different location. Correct as soon as possible or before the follow-up inspection on Friday, July 24.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed several containers of utensils and equipment stored on the floor in several locations.
violations.corrective_action: Cleaned equipment and utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items shall be stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches off the floor on NSF approved shelving units or dunnage racks. No food equipment or food may be stored on the floor. Discontinue storing these items on the floor. Correct prior to the follow-up on July 24.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squeeze bottles of pistachio sauce, chocolate sauce and lotus sauce stored throughout the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC labeled all squeezed bottles of pistachio, chocolate and lotus sauces during the inspection.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed containers with flour and sugar in the back of kitchen and boxes of chocolates in dry storage stored directly on the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PIC placed all aforementioned food on raised shelving.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter throughout of serving area.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PIC placed wiping cloth in sanitizer solution.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed cups without handle using as a dispensing utensils for all types of crunchy flakes.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC removed the cup from the containers of crunchy flakes and understands dispensing utensils should have a handle if stored inside food items.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Test Kit/Device for Chemical Sanitizer
violations.observation: There is no bleach test kit located in the facility for monitoring the concentration of the chemical sanitizing solutions.
violations.corrective_action: PIC purchased bleach test kit during the inspection for monitoring the concentration of the bleach sanitizing solution.
